title: I dont have money for ai
author: Moist_Show7700
selftext: I don’t have any money of my own to spend—or at least not enough—because I’m a minor, quite young in fact. I’m also a minor who develops games and other projects, often using AI. I need help quickly—any recommendations or resources that could help me continue developing effectively would be great.

Use Codex and prepare prompts in other AI (Gemini). So measure it twice and cut once.

comments.author: darrkestkniiight
comments.body: Might not be the response you're looking for but try not to use AI since your young, learning alot of those skills early on without relying on AI(especially if your interested in these types of things as a potential carrer) will be really helpful, when I was 10 (11 years ago) or so I used to code, make cheats for games, and learned how to hack into cameras, shut off people's wifi, etc.(black hat or gray hat stuff that I phased out of) since then I have wished I stuck with it because having to rely on AI for alot feels.. cheap? Learning things at a younger age is alot easier than later so I'd really suggest trying to learn things without relying on AI. Idk your skills or knowledge just giving my personal view on these things. No judgement against AI either, I actively use it for alot nowadays including at this moment literally. As for a more relevant answer to your question, I mostly used Chatgpt and Gemini for coding for free but they have alot of limitations. If you ever get the chance I'd say get a Claude subscription, ive been using it lately and it's a complete game changer.

comments.author: StellarSoupStudio
comments.body:
I would recommend learning the basics of game dev without ai since your still learning.

Learn how game engines work, try to make something like snake, or brick break from scratch.

You need to develop your vocabulary of how games work at a technical level if you want to be as efficient as possible with the limited LLM access you have.

[learncacademy.com](http://learncacademy.com) is where I got started, they're JavaScript courses were good back in the day, but there are plenty of other options.

You can definitely jump into gamedev with AI, but you'll be more effective if you work on your foundation first.

comments.author: Dhaupin
comments.body:
Good news, you don't need money for Ai. In fact I have never payed a single red cent for Ai. Here's what I use. All are cloud based with a Linux workspace, and work in a browser. You don't even need a pc. 

OpenHands Canvas - https://app.all-hands.dev/canvas/ - free deepseek 4.1 - 4 vcore 15gb Linux workspace (I use for - this is my daily driver, covers 95% of stuff)

Freebuff Cloud - https://freebuff.com/?ref=ref-626f6400-2154-41c0-b0e9-7e809c3282d5&via=rewards_link - free deepseek 4.1 fast max - 8 vcore 16gb Linux workspace (I use for - auditing, qc, vetting, merges, mitigates, refactors, and setting up bigger/deeper tasks)

Kilo Cloud - https://share.kilo.ai/mzXOIG4 - "openrouter free models router" or "auto free" pool (along with other free models) - 2 vcore 8gb Linux workspace (I use for - planning, research, writing specs, prds, etc)

Kilo cloud has low context models (256k), so you have to heavily leverage subagents there. Don't use their gas town stuff, just manually orchestrate.

Yes these technically come with a vps. But it often gets reallocated so it's not stable for hosting on. Previewing and testing however work great.

Docker works on openhands and kilo cloud. Prob won't on Freebuff until they allow it.

replies.author: Dhaupin
replies.body:
PS: I do a lot of multi agent and multi device stuff (95% via a phone). So to make it easier to orchestrate, you have 2 routes (among millions of others lol):

Vant - https://github.com/dhaupin/vant - mesh/horcrux based persistance, memory, orchestration, in repo. There's an open relay and dashboard in development at https://brain.creadev.org (pls submit issues to vant repo)

Gistory - https://gistory.creadev.org/ - local to local sync prompt/notes keeper. Think encrypted brave browser sync, for prompts/notes. If you don't trust this, the sync engine npm is available to build your own at https://npmjs.com/package/gistory-sync

For GPU I use Google colab. It has decent tiers available, and some Google subscription (don't remember which) unlocks the higher tier GPU ram. It's python based so works well with existing cloud agent <> vps <> rendering flows (ie blender).
